To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the translocation of metals from bark to leaves of willows is important, and that Mn concentrations in bark can be a good indicator for delayed budburst of willows.

(1) the translocation of metals from bark to shoots is an important mechanism for the uptake of metals from sediments in willows, (2) the translocation process is particularly important for Mn and (3) the translocation is related to delayed budburst of willows

the translocation of metals from bark to leaves of willows is an important mechanism for the accumulation of metals in leaves, and that delayed budburst is a direct result of high Mn concentrations in willow bark.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of bark in the metal dynamics of willow plants.
the fate of heavy metals in contaminated willow stands.
the fate of Cd, Zn, and Mn in the bark, the translocation of these metals to leaves, and their impact on budburst in willow.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
delayed budburst is a consequence of the high Mn concentrations in bark, which in turn are a consequence of the translocation of Mn into the bark from the roots.
the translocation of Cd and Zn to shoots of willow is limited, but that the translocation from bark to shoots of Mn is important.
the delayed or restricted bud burst of Salix cinera in the contaminated plots was caused by high bark concentrations of Mn.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
delayed budburst is a result of high Mn concentrations in willow cuttings grown on contaminated soils.
Mn in the bark is the main cause for delayed budburst and that the high Cd concentrations in the bark are not a direct cause of the delayed budburst.
the delayed budburst of Salix cuttings is related to Mn concentrations in the wood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
willow bark is a dynamic compartment that is not a long-term sink of metals.
willows on contaminated soils may not be suitable for the phytoremediation of sediments with high Mn concentrations.
the hydrological regime of a contaminated site is a major factor determining the uptake and translocation of heavy metals in plants.
